findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.citation_text:
3-307.11 Miscellaneous Sources of Contamination. FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 - 3-306. 

Boxes of plastic to-go containers were observed on the floor in the backstock area where the produce department stores their containers. The PIC was shown and the situation discussed. The items were moved during the inspection to correct. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are stored up off of the ground at all times in the facility.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

Multiple hand sinks throughout the facility were observed with missing or cracking seals round the sinks. The individual sinks were shown to the PIC and they were instructed to repair/re-seal the sinks to the walls to maintain a smooth and easily cleanable surface at all times.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

An employee was observed to wash their hands and use their bare hands to turn off the faucet. Education was conducted and the PIC is instructed to ensure education trickles down to all employees and that they are conducting correct procedures at all times.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.citation_text:
5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use.

1) In two locations the hand sinks are blocked by equipment. Locations include the produce walk in cooler and the sink at the end of the oven line. The PICs were shown and moved the blocking items to correct. Ensure that all hand sinks are maintained accessible at all times to promote regulate and consistent use.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

The three part sink was observed being remade during this inspection. The employee was mixing hot water with the pre-metered solution. The solution was tested and did not register on the inspector’s test strips. Education was conducted. The dispenser is designed and adjusted so that the solution coming out of the equipment is at the correct concentration and diluting it reduces its efficacy to ineffective levels. The sink was remade to correct. Ensure that education is trickled down and that all staff can use the relevant equipment correctly in the facility.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety (TCS) Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. 

Beef and chicken in the Asian Market are observed on the counter of the prep cooler out of temperature control. It was found that the items were removed from the cooler approximately an hour before observation. Internal temperatures were observed at 60F. Education was conducted and the items allowed to be moved back into the cooler. Ensure that foods are not left out for prolonged periods of time without temperature control.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.citation_text:
6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination.

At several locations in this facility employee related foods and drink were observed intermixed with foods and ingredients intended for consumers. The locations were shown to the PIC and they were instructed to designate a place for employee foods to be stored so that they would not be a concern for contaminating consumer foods. The items were moved during this inspection to correct. Drinks in the facility should be in a cups that have lids and straws as well.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

The sani bucket in the sushi and asian market area is observed to not register on the inspector’s test strips. The PIC was shown and replaced the buckets during the inspection to correct the immediate violation. Ensure that all sanitizers are maintained at correct concentration at all times in the facility.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

1) The pineapple slicer in the area to the west side of the hot line is observed with dry food debris on it. When asked the nearby employee stated that they were not sure the last time that it had been used as it wasted a lot of pineapple and they have been slicing by hand for some time. This leads to the conclusion that it was not properly cleaned when it was put away and left soiled for a long period of time. 2) Multiple large buckets are used for preparing tea (per the PIC) and are stored on the shelves with remaining tea residue on them. They are also still partially wet from cleaning. The PIC had the items cleaned during this inspection to correct. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are completely cleaned prior to storage.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety (TCS) Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. 

The display cooler used for cake slices along the service line is observed with a holding temperature of 57F. Most items in this cooler are not TCS foods and so are not a concern. There is a box of sour cream packets in the container though that bares a label requiring refrigeration. This was discussed with the PIC and the sour cream packets discarded to correct the immediate concern. The PIC indicated that they would be putting in a work order for the cooler moving forward.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.111(C) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (C) Using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13.

Several flies (at least 8-10) are observed by the mop sink and adjacent tanks. The PIC was shown and instructed to contact their pest control agency (EcoLab) for maintinance. They did mention that EcoLab had already been planning on starting a fly based plan in the facility. This should probably be pushed forward and implemented immediately. The normal follow-up schedule would land on a weekend and will be pushed back to the following Monday.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
findings.citation_text:
3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D).

Multiple rags used for wiping counters are observed stored on the counters in the facility. These items were pointed out to the PIC and discussed. They should be stored between uses in their sani buckets that are maintained at proper concentration. The rags were moved to the sani buckets to correct.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

The hand sink in the produce walk in cooler/prep area is observed with a gap forming in the caulking sealing it to the wall. The PIC was shown and instructed to reseal prior to the next routine inspection. Ensure a that all facilities are smooth and easily cleanable where water and moisture is consistently in abundance.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. 

One of the doors on the employee side of the display cooler used for pasta salad has several pieces of duck tape being used as a repair medium. Duck tape is not an approved method of making repairs as it allows for mold/pathogen growth. The location was discussed with the PIC and they are instructed to repair properly prior to the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.citation_text:
6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels.

The paper towel dispenser next to the fryers is without paper towels during this inspection. The PIC was shown and had the roll replaced during this inspection to correct the violation. Ensure that all hand sinks are properly supplied at all times.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
(REPEAT x3) 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Multiple utensils throughout the storage areas are observed soiled. They do not appear to have been completely cleaned prior to being placed in storage or ready for use locations. The PIC was shown each item as it was observed and the items moved back to dish for re-cleaning. This has been an ongoing observed situation for several inspections in a row and should be remedied by management. Education and oversight are HIGHLY suggested at this time. Ensure that all dishes and utensils are completely cleaned prior to storage and future use. A spot check will be  conducted moving forward to ensure that all dishes are being completely cleaned on a consistent basis moving forward.

findings.citation_text:

Multiple sani buckets in the facility are observed to either not register on the inspector’s test strips or to register low. findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
(REPEAT x2) 4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Multiple dishes appear to have been put away with food debris or residues still present. The PIC was shown and the items moved back to dish for recleaning. This is the third inspection in a row where food contact items (dishes/utensils, ect.) appear to have this issue. A conversation with the dish washers is HIGHLY suggested. Ensure that education/training is completed and that the food contact surfaces are completely cleaned prior to storage.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. 

Cut melons in the end cap cooler at the end of the produce section of the facility are observed with internal temperatures ranging from 48.8F-52.3F. The PIC was shown and educated on the common variability between the built in thermometers for the open sided coolers and the food temperatures in these coolers. The items were discarded during this inspection to correct the immediate violation. A similar violation was noted on the previous routine inspection. This is a repeated situation. Ensure that coolers are monitored and the TCS foods maintained cold at all times.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned. 

1) A knife in the sushi preparation area is being stored between the prep cooler and the wall. 2) A pair of tongs are stored through the rack in the small walk in cooler next to the Asian food prep location. It is in contact with a metal section that has a white powder contaminating it. Both items were shown to the PIC and removed during this inspection to correct. Ensure that all in use utensils are stored in ways so that there is not a concern of the food contact surfaces becoming contaminated.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-303.11: (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. 

From the beginning of the inspection until brought up nearly an hour into the inspection there were not any observable sani buckets available for use throughout the food prep and handling areas of the kitchen. The PIC was consulted and buckets were produced to correct. Ensure that sanitizers are ready for use at all times that foods are prepared/handled.
